assumptions: Rigid horizontal table edge 18–22 mm thick, without a strongly rounded or fragile edge
PLA density and CAD mass distribution estimate reset tendency; physical reset and sound remain untested
Print on the flat 32 mm side with 0.4 mm nozzle, 0.2 mm layers, three or more perimeters, and at least 20% infill

components.form: One continuous side-printable lantern silhouette with open edge saddle
components.interfaces: Upper throat rolls on tabletop corner; lower jaw clears underside except at striker
components.name: Lantern cage and saddle
components.placement: Spans the table edge with globe inboard and cap outboard
components.purpose: Carries all loads as one rigid printed part

components.form: Two coplanar broad landing pads integrated into the inboard upper rail
components.interfaces: Both faces meet the tabletop together at rest
components.name: Twin landing pads
components.placement: Inboard of the rounded throat, separated along the table edge
components.purpose: Create the broad return knock and stable rest

components.form: Support-safe hemispherical crown fused to the lower jaw
components.interfaces: Sole underside stop at the pressed pose
components.name: Underside striker
components.placement: Inboard lower jaw beneath the tabletop

components.interfaces: Rigidly joined to outboard lever arm
components.name: Press cap
components.placement: Outboard of throat near the envelope end
components.purpose: Provides an obvious press target and lever arm

concept.intended_interaction: Slide the open saddle over a rigid 18–22 mm table edge until the twin pads rest on top. Press the broad outboard cap: the rounded R6 throat rolls about the edge toward a nominal 12 degree pose on a 20 mm table and the 6 mm nub reaches the underside first. Release; the inboard globe biases the body home and the paired 12 by 8 mm pads are intended to land together.
concept.signature_decision: A visibly lantern-like, one-piece C-saddle makes the two contact scales legible: one tiny amber underside nub for the tap and two broad base pads for the return knock. The oversized inboard globe is functional ballast, not ornament.
concept.summary: A single-piece camping-lantern rocker that saddles a table edge. One press rolls its rounded throat to tap the underside with a 6 mm nub; release lets the inboard-weighted globe roll home onto two broad pads.
concept.title: Ember Knock
unresolved_risks: Actual sound contrast, loudness, and timbre require an exact physical print and listening test
Reset depends on real infill, material density, table friction, and edge profile
Warp or elephant foot may prevent simultaneous pad landing
Table thickness outside 18–22 mm can change or defeat contact order

research.claim_limits: CAD can establish envelope, contact geometry, nominal kinematics, wall thickness, mesh integrity, and an estimated inboard mass bias. It cannot establish audible pitch, loudness, timbre distinction, durability, friction, or successful reset in a physical print.
research.design_basis: Sonora Reed inventor review: use a constant-section side-print stance, at least 3 mm structural sections, R6 rolling throat, twin 12x8 mm pads, true 6 mm striker crown, and a visibly inboard mass concentration.
research.fit_basis: Declared table range is 18–22 mm with nominal 20 mm; contact angle varies with thickness and approximately 12 degrees is only the nominal case.
research.safety: Use only on stable rigid horizontal furniture; avoid glass, fragile, strongly beveled, or unstable edges; keep hands and face clear beneath the striker.
